blogs.title: Beyond Sepsis: Unmasking Complement-Mediated HUS After Dog Bites
blogs.description: This post explores the deceptive clinical course of *Capnocytophaga canimorsus* bacteremia, where initial septic shock and DIC can obscure a subsequent, life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). We will discuss why the 'late' onset of hemolysis and thrombocytopenia in a recovering septic patient should trigger an immediate TMA workup, even when classic signs of HUS appear absent initially.

blogs.title: Normal C3/C4 Does Not Rule Out Atypical HUS: A Diagnostic Pitfall
blogs.description: Focusing on the diagnostic criteria for complement-mediated HUS (CM-HUS), this article debunks the common misconception that normal baseline complement levels (C3/C4) exclude the diagnosis. Using this case, we analyze why traditional screening tests fail in acute settings and emphasize the necessity of advanced functional assays (e.g., AH50) and genetic testing when clinical suspicion for CM-HUS remains high despite normal basic serology.

blogs.title: The Eculizumab Dilemma: Balancing Terminal Complement Blockade Against Encapsulated Bacteria
blogs.description: Managing CM-HUS in the setting of active or recent infection with encapsulated organisms like *Neisseria* or *Capnocytophaga* presents a unique therapeutic tension. This post reviews the risks of administering eculizumab during or immediately after bacteremia, outlining best practices for vaccination timing, antimicrobial prophylaxis, and strategic delays to minimize mortality from overwhelming post-splenectomy-like sepsis while treating the TMA.

blogs.title: Pitfalls in Differentiating TTP from CM-HUS: Why ADAMTS13 Matters More Than You Think
blogs.description: When faced with MAHA and thrombocytopenia, distinguishing between Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) and CM-HUS is critical. This educational piece uses the case's timeline to highlight how ADAMTS13 activity levels act as the definitive pivot point. It discusses why Plasma Exchange serves as a bridge rather than a cure in CM-HUS and warns against misdiagnosing infection-triggered TMA as autoimmune hemolytic anemia based solely on a false-positive Coombs test.
